sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: Before the storm, I put cushions on the garden bench every evening.

sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: Mara brought stories about people she met at the dock. Sol told us about things he had made.

sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: Slowly, their visits became less frequent. Sometimes I waited beside an empty bench.

sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: "Perhaps they don't enjoy our stories anymore," I thought.

sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: Eventually, I put the spare cushions away.

sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: Today, I learned why they had stayed away. Mara was working when our gatherings took place. Sol thought no one would want to hear his story.

sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: I had assumed that fewer visits meant my friends no longer cared about the garden. I should have asked what was keeping them away.

sources.title: The Empty Bench

sources.text: Pip helped us find a way to share our stories again.

sources.title: The Empty Bench
sources.author: by Grandma
sources.text: I brought the cushions out again.

sources.text: I was spreading a cloth over the garden table when the wind snatched one corner from my hand.

sources.title: The Windy Picnic

sources.text: Sol caught it before it knocked over a jug of water.

sources.title: The Windy Picnic
sources.author: by Grandma · an older garden story
sources.text: "We'll need to secure the corners," he said.

sources.title: The Windy Picnic

sources.text: Mara fetched four smooth stones from beside the path. We placed one on each corner and set out our picnic.

sources.title: The Windy Picnic

sources.text: The wind ruffled our hair and rattled the leaves, but the cloth stayed put.

sources.title: The Windy Picnic
sources.author: by Grandma · an older garden story
sources.text: "Next time, I'll bring a heavier tablecloth," I said.

sources.title: The Windy Picnic

sources.text: "Bring the same cake," said Sol.

sources.title: The Windy Picnic

sources.text: A boy carried a flute onto my boat. He kept it tucked beneath his arm while the other passengers found their seats.

sources.title: The Unexpected Duet
sources.author: by Mara · an older garden story
sources.text: "Would you like to play something?" I asked.

sources.title: The Unexpected Duet
sources.author: by Mara · an older garden story
sources.text: He hesitated, then lifted the flute. The first notes were so quiet that I could hardly hear them.

sources.title: The Unexpected Duet

sources.text: A whistle answered from the back of the boat. An older passenger had recognised the tune.

sources.title: The Unexpected Duet
sources.author: by Mara · an older garden story
sources.text: The boy started again. This time, they played together.

sources.title: The Unexpected Duet

sources.text: Sol had brought his tools and a ladder. An intact spare tile rested on a shelf beside the bakery.

sources.text: The repair had prevented the flour from getting wet. Rina used it to bake the bread she had promised. Fixing one tile had helped her keep that promise.

sources.title: Sol’s prepared ending: Rina’s visit
sources.author: Prepared words for Sol
sources.text: Later, Rina brought me a loaf of bread to say thank you. I had thought it was only a small repair. It had mattered to her.

sources.title: A promise to Grandma
sources.author: Pip's adventure
sources.text: On an earlier visit, Grandma had given Pip a lantern seed. They had promised to plant it together before dark today. Pip put the seed in his backpack and set off for her garden.

sources.title: A promise to Grandma
sources.author: Pip's adventure
sources.text: Last night's storm had washed away the footbridge. At the river, Pip stopped and took out Grandma's letter. She had written it before the storm.

sources.title: A promise to Grandma
sources.author: Pip's adventure
sources.text: "Mara and Sol hardly visit anymore. I think they don't enjoy coming to the garden now. I miss hearing their stories."

sources.title: Mara's story can travel

sources.text: Mara stood on the dock with a sheet of paper in her hand.

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "Is that a story?" Pip asked.

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "One I wrote for Grandma's garden," Mara replied.

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "Grandma thinks you don't enjoy going there anymore."

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: Mara lowered the page. "I miss it. But my work hours changed before the storm. I used to finish before the storytelling began. Now I have to wait for the last boat to return. By then, everyone at the garden has gone home."

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "Could you leave a little earlier?"

sources.title: Mara's story can travel
sources.author: At the passenger dock
sources.text: "I have an obligation to the passengers," Mara said. "I need to help them get safely off the boat."

sources.title: The boat and the broken bridge
sources.author: Grandma’s maintenance note
sources.text: These are my two reusable footbridge sections. You may use them to repair the crossing. The two ropes in this marked box are for fastening the bridge. —Grandma

sources.title: The boat and the broken bridge
sources.author: Grandma’s maintenance note
sources.text: Join the two bridge sections to make a footbridge. Look for the posts where the banks are close enough for the deck to reach both sides. Secure one end to each bank before anyone walks across.

sources.title: The boat and the broken bridge
sources.author: Grandma’s maintenance note
sources.text: My small boat can carry the seed, but it cannot carry Pip. Load the seed at the yellow launch. Steer around the rock to my blue landing, then give me the seed. I will prepare the soil and wait for Pip to plant it with me.

sources.title: The boat and the broken bridge
sources.author: Grandma’s maintenance note
sources.text: Keep the boat's route clear. The bridge stays in place so everyone can return.

sources.title: The boat and the broken bridge
sources.author: Grandma’s maintenance note
sources.text: The seed stays dark in a boat or a hand. Its lantern-flower grows only after its roots reach the hill's soil.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: Everyone had stepped off the last boat except a boy holding a paper bird.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "Are you waiting for someone?" I asked.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: He shook his head.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "This is for my grandmother. My sister made it, but she's too ill to come. I promised my sister I'd keep it safe."

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: One wing was torn.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: I reached toward the bird, but he pulled it closer.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "Would you like some help?" I asked.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: He hesitated. Then he held out the bird.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: I fetched some tape from the dock office. Together, we mended the wing.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: When he stepped onto the dock, he held the bird carefully in both hands.

sources.title: The Torn Wing
sources.author: by Mara
sources.text: "Now I can tell my grandmother how we fixed it," he said.

sources.title: A story reaches Grandma
sources.author: Pip and Grandma
sources.text: "Mara still wants to come. But she's working at the dock while we're telling stories here. She asked me to share this with you."

sources.title: A story reaches Grandma
sources.author: Pip and Grandma
sources.text: "I thought she'd stopped enjoying the garden. I should have asked her what had happened. Let's read what she sent."
